messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] data_cleaning_file function when using "SPT"
parts:
Hi Xinting,

As far as I can see arguments data_cleaning_file and sleepwindowType do not interact with each other inside the GGIR code. 

Could it be that by setting sleepwindowType to "SPT" those nights are excluded regardless of whether the nights are specified in data_cleaning_file?

If not, can you explain in more detail what you mean by "...did not work" and summarise the number of nights you see in the output when you systematically test each of the possible scenarios:

  1. sleepwindowType = "SPT" data_cleaning_file used
  2. sleepwindowType = "TimeInBed" data_cleaning_file used
  3. sleepwindowType = "SPT" data_cleaning_file NOT used
  4. sleepwindowType = "TimeInBed" data_cleaning_file NOT used

Thanks,
Vincent

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] data_cleaning_file function when using "SPT"
parts: Also I have another question related to the cleaning: In our study some subjects did not provided enough sleep log for all the days recorded. I kept those days blank in the sleep log. The days without sleep logs cannot be reflected in the final night summaries and average summaries. I am retrieving the results from QC summaries and cleaning the days on my ends. Please let me know if you have a better idea.

Yes, I think you identified a good solution. GGIR provides two version of the output:
  1. results folder: these are typically cleaned, which means that all days with do not meet inclusion criteria are removed, and if you use a sleeplog then all nights without a sleeplog will also be removed. I do this because I am not sure whether it is informative to mix two different sleep methods (with and without sleeplog) in the same person-level summary measures. In GGIR part 5 I have no been this strict about the availability of sleeplog method, because in GGIR part 5 is not on sleep assessment but on capturing the waking hours of the day.
  2. QC folder: all days are included and it is up to you to clean and summarise the data as you prefer.

Approach 1 aims to be the easiest default approach relevant to most GGIR users. However, if you feel approach 2 better aligns with your research interests then yes definitely go for that. I created it, exactly because I knew there would be need for a less cleaned-up version of the data.

Best, Vincent

parts:
Dear Vincent

I'm posting here because I feel this is somewhat related. 

Do I understand correctly that I can manually exclude nights by specifiying the individual (by providing the ID) and the night in the Data cleaning file if I think that the data quality in these nights is not sufficient?

5.6.6 Data cleaning file

The package allows some adjustments to be made after data quality check. The data_cleaning_file argument allows you to specify individuals and nights for whom part4 should entirely rely on the guider (for example if we decide to use sleep log only information). The first column of this file should have header ID and there should be a column relyonguider_part4 to specify the night. The data_cleaning_file allows you to tell GGIR which person(s) and night(s) should be omitted in part 4. The the night numbers to be excluded should be listed in a column night_part4 as header.

So then i would make e.g. a CSV file with the first rows containing the headers "ID", "relyonguider_part4", "night_part4"?

It seems to me, that "relyonguider_part4" and "night_part4" describe the same thing?

So I could write a CSV file with 
"ID", "relyonguider_part4", "night_part4"
subject_1, 4, 4
subject_1, 5, 5

Or can I specify several nights in some form of a list?
"ID", "relyonguider_part4", "night_part4"
"subject_1", 4, c(4, 5, 6)

Thanks for your help!

I do this because I am not sure whether it is informative to mix two different sleep methods (with and without sleeplog) in the same person-level summary measures.   2. QC folder: all days are included and it is up to you to clean and summarise the data as you prefer.

messages.author: 05de4f382b390d3d
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] data_cleaning_file function when using "SPT"
parts:
Hi Christian,

This would be the correct format:

"ID", "relyonguider_part4", "night_part4"
subject_1, 4, 4
subject_1, 5, 5

"relyonguider_part4" would make that for the specified night, the guider for sleep analysis would be trusted (see section on guiders in the vignette). Otherwise, "night_part4" would make that the specified night is not included in the part 4 reports.

Best,
Jairo
